Working principle

Finished size differs from cut size

Before calculating fabric length, decide which edges will be sewn, how much width is usable and which way the grain and print run. The tools show arithmetic; your sketch decides whether the layout is practical.

01 / Method & sources

Three notes before cutting

  1. 01

    Measure the finished object and mark each edge treatment.

  2. 02

    Decide cut dimensions and grain or print direction.

  3. 03

    Arrange pieces across usable fabric width; explain any extra length.

03 / Guides

Eight guides from sketch to buying note

Learn finished size, seam allowance, fabric width, grain, panel layout, prints, shrinkage and planning notes. The examples are reproducible arithmetic.

01 / 08

Finished size versus cut size

Similar-looking measurements can produce different finished objects. Start with the result you want, then allow for joins.

Read guide ↗
02 / 08

Seam allowances and hems do different jobs

Joining two pieces differs from folding a visible outer edge. Plan each edge as part of the pattern.

Read guide ↗
03 / 08

Read grain direction and usable width

A cutting calculation works only when the pattern may be oriented across the available fabric width.

Read guide ↗
04 / 08

Lay out rectangular fabric panels

Find how many pieces fit across each row before multiplying fabric length. The layout is transparent and deliberately simple.

Read guide ↗
05 / 08

Estimate edging tape from perimeter

For a rectangle, perimeter starts the tape estimate; joins and allowances still need recording.

Read guide ↗
06 / 08

Plan repeat patterns and print direction

Printed fabric can require more length than a plain-fabric layout suggests.

Read guide ↗
07 / 08

Prepare fabric and check shrinkage

Dimensional change after care can undo careful arithmetic. Follow the care label and remeasure the fabric.

Read guide ↗
08 / 08

Make a cutting plan before buying

A one-page note keeps finished size, cut size, orientation and purchase length connected.

Read guide ↗
